posts.pinComment: If prompts are your shadow codebase: I keep a short ops checklist (approvals + publish planes + STOP). Comment OPS for the link.
posts.text:
"We'll fix the prompt later" is how you build a hidden programming language nobody reviews.

A prompt is not vibes.

It is behavior under uncertainty.

Later never gets a calendar invite.

Later becomes folklore: "ask it this way, it works better" - tribal knowledge wearing a productivity costume.

If you wouldn't ship code without a second pair of eyes, don't ship prompt changes without a trail.

Version it. Name the failure mode. Test the edge case you don't want to explain to a customer.

I am not anti-speed.

I am anti-mystery.

If your team is standing up agents and the governance layer is still "we'll clean this up" - DM me. I implement agent workflows with real review trails, not vibes.

If you're hiring for growth / AI implementation / agent systems where prompts are treated like shipping surface area - I'm open to the right role. DM the JD or one-line scope.

#AI #Engineering #Operations #Product #Prompting

posts.pinComment: Gates + approvals + STOP: Comment OPS for the doc. Founders fixing "human in the loop" theater - same.
posts.text:
"Human in the loop" is not a moral sticker.

It is a workflow.

If humans always approve because they're scared to be slow, you didn't add safety.

You added latency and called it governance.

A real loop has teeth: what gets blocked, what gets escalated, what gets logged, and who is allowed to say no without a career penalty.

Otherwise the human is decoration.

And the model knows it.

Build the loop you'd want if you were the one signing.

Founders and ops leads: if you need someone to design approval planes for agent + social + publish workflows (not a slide - a runnable rule set) - DM me the use case in one paragraph.

If you're hiring for AI product / implementation / growth engineering where governance is part of the job, not an afterthought - I want to see it. DM the role title or link.

#AI #Governance #Risk #Operations #Leadership

posts.pinComment: Vendor + workflow reality: Comment OPS for the short ops checklist.
posts.text:
The vendor deck promised freedom.

The export screen said "coming soon."

If your workflow dies when you change vendors, you didn't build leverage.

You built a lease.

Portable doesn't mean purist.

It means: artifacts, interfaces, and decisions that survive a Tuesday renegotiation.

Can you export the rules?

Can someone else run the checklist without your hero employee?

If the honest answer is no, say it out loud in the room.

That sentence saves money later.

I like builders who treat exit as a feature - not because they're leaving, because they're not children about dependency.

Agency principals and technical founders: if you're shipping agent + automation stacks for clients and you want manifests, fallbacks, and handoff docs that survive staff churn - DM me. I like implementation work that respects margin.

If you're hiring someone who bridges architecture and delivery for AI workflows - growth, platform, or implementation - send the role. I care about boring portability.

#Automation #Architecture #SaaS #AI #Operations

posts.pinComment: Agents + single source of truth: Comment OPS for the doc.
posts.text:
Ten parallel chats are not ten times productivity.

They're ten drafts of reality that still need an owner.

I run serious work out of repos for a reason.

Committed text is a merge path.

Threads are weather.

If two agents disagree, that's not a vibe problem.

It's a contract problem.

Who resolves it, with what evidence, and where does the decision live tomorrow morning?

If you can't answer that, you're not orchestrating.

You're improvising in stereo.

Companies rolling out multi-agent setups and hitting "everyone has a different answer" - DM me. I implement orchestration patterns people can actually run (agents as contracts, not vibes).

If you're hiring for AI systems / platform / growth engineering with real orchestration scope - that's the role I want. DM the JD summary.

#AI #Agents #Workflow #Engineering #BuildingInPublic

posts.pinComment: Aligning leadership + ship log: Comment OPS for the seven questions doc.
posts.text:
Slide decks get applause.

Deploy logs get dates.

The story you tell leadership should not contradict the deploy log.

If it does, you don't have alignment.

You have a polite fog.

Fog feels safe in the meeting.

It is expensive in production.

I respect teams that can say: here is what shipped, here is what broke, here is what we learned, here is what we are funding next.

No myth-making.

No hero arcs.

Just the work, with timestamps.

That's the kind of environment where AI help is actually additive - because the ground truth exists.

Executives and founders bridging AI investment with operational truth - DM me if you want a second brain on sequencing: what to gate, what to prove, what to automate next.

If you're hiring a senior growth / AI / product-leaning builder who lives in that gap between narrative and deploy - let's talk. DM the mandate.

#Leadership #Product #Engineering #AI #Culture
